findings.text: Provides a pre-boot routine that walks a stream of exception-frame records, validates shared header records, and applies shadow-call-stack rewriting to described code locations, supporting an optional validation-only pass before the mutating pass and reporting distinct failures for malformed headers or operand encodings.

A shared header is accepted only with augmentation tag zR demanding pointer-format description, single-byte alignment factors, return register thirty, unit augmentation length, and a PC-relative signed width of either four or eight bytes; the width choice governs later record parsing and the alignment factor scales later location advances.

Description interpretation maintains a current code address derived from its start field, consumes a single-byte augmentation length, then consumes operation bytes: sized advance forms move the address by scaled deltas, several definition and restore forms skip one or two variable-length operands, state save and restore plus no-operation and two high ranges leave the address unchanged, while the return-state toggle triggers a rewrite slightly behind the current address when mutating; unknown codes or multi-byte augmentation lengths fail.

Location rewriting exchanges only two authenticated-return encodings for their shadow-stack push and pop counterparts and otherwise leaves memory untouched to tolerate imprecise unwinder state; after a successful exchange it cleans the affected line toward unification or coherency using a build-selected cache operation.
Variable-length operand skipping advances a cursor past continuation-marked bytes until a terminating byte, decreasing the remaining budget accordingly and returning the updated budget.

Exception-frame storage begins with a length word where zero ends iteration and all-ones is rejected, followed by a discriminator that is zero for shared headers and nonzero for descriptions; shared headers carry version, tag, alignment factors, return register, augmentation size and pointer format, while descriptions carry either 32-bit start and range plus trailing bytes or 64-bit start and range plus trailing bytes.

Call-frame operation numbers assign zero to no-operation, ten and eleven to state save and restore, two to four to increasingly wide location advances, and forty-five to return-state negation; values sixty-four to one twenty-seven advance by embedded delta, one twenty-eight to one ninety-one skip an operand, and one ninety-two to two fifty-five are ignored.

Pointer-format bytes combine a PC-relative base of sixteen with eleven to select four-byte signed addresses or twelve to select eight-byte signed addresses; the two rewrite triggers are fixed words 0xd503233f and 0xd50323bf while their replacements are fixed words 0xf800865e and 0xf85f8e5e respectively.

Early relocation adds the displacement to every relative dynamic entry target, then when compressed relocation support is enabled and displacement is nonzero it processes a mixed stream where even entries establish a new base word and odd entries act as maps applying the displacement to selected following words.

Identity-map CPU helper installs a reserved upper-table base supplied by the caller, adjusts another supplied base by the table offset, publishes it to the upper translation base register, orders with an instruction barrier, and returns.

Temporary larger-address switch disables address translation, programs the lower translation base to a supplied table, enables larger-address mode in translation control with intermediate size taken from the memory-model feature field, invalidates stage-one entries with ordering barriers, then restores translation enablement.

Identity-map refresh for larger addresses builds a provisional map without shared bits in a scratch area, runs from it while clearing and rebuilding the original map with the same granularity but safe descriptors, switches back to the rebuilt map, and finally erases the provisional area; device-tree mappings are not recreated.

Initial identity construction reserves one page beyond the supplied directory for further tables, derives text and data protections with a caller mask removed, and creates two contiguous identity ranges covering code through early data as read-execute and early data through image end as writable.

Device-tree staging maps at most a bounded size starting at the supplied physical address into the identity area using a static page-aligned table pool, truncating before the kernel image when overlapping, issuing a store barrier, and returning the original address as a pointer.

Primary early-mapping entry clears uninitialized storage and provisional tables, locates the chosen node to apply feature overrides, lowers address width or table depth when large-address support is absent, widens upper-table size when beneficial, derives randomized displacement from physical alignment plus firmware seed with erratum-gated non-global selection, optionally refreshes the identity map for larger addresses, and finally creates the kernel mapping at the displaced virtual base.
Non-global mapping permission is denied only on two listed ThunderX families and revisions associated with a hardware erratum and allowed on all other processors.
A single global boolean records whether dynamically patched shadow-call-stack support is active.

Place-relative references are stored as volatile signed displacements in a dedicated init read-only section through a union overlaying a native pointer; a helper yields null for zero displacement and otherwise adds the displacement to its own storage address.

Host-side object checker maps a supplied file, detects endianness mismatch from its identification byte, walks relocation sections that target allocated non-executable data, and rewrites absolute 64-bit entries found in designated place-relative read-only data to place-relative form while rejecting such entries elsewhere.

On encountering a forbidden absolute relocation the checker reports the target name, closes, deletes the mapped file, and exits with failure; it also exits with failure when arguments are missing or when open, status query, or mapping of the input fails.

Per-task pointer-authentication key control validates hardware support for address and generic keys and rejects compatibility threads, reinitializes all user keys when given zero, otherwise checks the request mask against supported keys and reseeds each selected instruction, data, and generic key from randomness before installing them.

Per-task authentication enablement keeps a saved control word, translates public key selectors into enable bits with warnings on unknown bits, and under disabled preemption replaces the selected bits with newly requested values, pushing the result to hardware immediately when affecting the running task; a companion query reconstructs the public mask from the saved word with the same support and compatibility guards.
